Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:112928
Court No. - 74

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 21459 of 2023
Applicant :- Ashok Singh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Siddhartha Baghel,Prateek Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant, is taken on record.

2. Heard Shri Siddhartha Baghel, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Ravi Kant Kushawaha,
learned A.G.A. for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been moved on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.026 of 2022, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 409, 120-B I.P.C., Police Station Hathinala, District Sonebhadra during pendency of the trial.

4. The F.I.R. of the present case was lodged against six owners of the four wheelers (non-applicant)
and as per allegation on the basis of forged documents, they got released their vehicle in their favour.
5.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is not named in the F.I.R. and his name was surfaced during investigation after four months and on the basis of information furnished by the police informer, he was arrested and on the basis of his confessional statement, he was made Ashok Singh vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132129771/
1 accused in the present matter.

sentences.text:
He next submits that except the confessional statement of the accused applicant, there is no evidence against him on record, which can show that the applicant was either broker in the R.T.O. Office or he represented himself as one of the clerk of the R.T.O.
Office and neither there is any allegation nor there is any evidence on record, which can show that he either prepared the alleged forged documents or handed over the same to the respective owner of the vehicles.

He further submits that the applicant is having criminal history of six other cases,
which have been explained in para 30 of the affidavit and para 3 of the supplementary affidavit filed in support of the present bail application.

He next submits that the applicant in the present matter is in jail since 24.04.2023.
6.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that co-accused Vijendra Kumar Alias Guddu has already been enlarged on bail by Bench of this Court vide order dated 02.03.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.7356 of 2023, which has been annexed as Annexure No.3 to the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application and the case of applicant is at par with him,
therefore, he may be released on bail..

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.7356 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the applicant is the broker in the R.T.O. Office and represented himself as one of the clerk of the R.T.O. Office and helped the vehicle owners in preparing the forged documents of the vehicle but he could not dispute the fact that except the confessional statement of the accused-applicant, there is no other evidence against him on record.
8. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.
9. Applicant was not named in the F.I.R. and his name was surfaced during investigation after four months and when he was arrested, he confessed his guilt.

Although there is allegation against him that he is broker in the R.T.O. Office and represented himself as one of the clerk of the R.T.O. Office and also preparing some forged documents and on the basis of those documents, vehicles were released in favour of their owners but it reflects from the record that except confessional statement there is no evidence against him on record.

Applicant is having criminal history of six other cases,
which have been explained in para 30 of the affidavit and para 3 of the supplementary affidavit filed in support of the present bail application and he in the present matter is in jail since 24.04.2023,
therefore, I am of the considered view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. In the light of discussions made above, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant- Ashok Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless her personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
